title: What a flow cannot do, and how one extra dimension fixes it
summary: Flows of ODEs cannot cross, so a Neural ODE on the line cannot represent x to minus x, and a planar one cannot unlink two nested rings. Adding one augmented coordinate lets the trajectories pass around each other. These figures show the obstruction, the exact lifted flows that avoid it, and what learned models do.

media.alt: Three panels in a row. Left, titled 1-D flow curves never cross: red dots where minus x0 would have to end, and about twenty blue curves of x against time from 0 to 1 that converge toward but never reach plus or minus 0.9. Middle, titled augmented flow, half circles: concentric half circles in the plane of x and an augmented coordinate u. Right, titled best a monotone map can do, mean squared error 0.338: a grey line for the target minus x and an orange flat line at zero for the best nondecreasing fit.

read_the_figure.question: Can the flow of this model map the inputs to the targets, and if not, which structural change makes it possible?
read_the_figure.axes: Left: time against x(t). Middle: x(t) (horizontal) against the augmented coordinate u(t) (vertical). Right: input x against the output of a monotone map. Rings figures: x1 against x2 for two classes; learned decision regions are filled in blue and red; the winding-number histogram counts 40 random planar flows.
look_at: Left panel: in one dimension two trajectories that start at different points can never meet, so the order of the points is preserved; the red dots show the endpoints that x to -x would require, which no curve reaches.
Middle: in the augmented plane the same points move along half circles, so x0 arrives at -x0 by passing through the extra dimension; the title gives the maximum endpoint error 3.8e-12.
Right: the best nondecreasing map for the target -x is the zero map, with mean squared error 0.338, the same as predicting zero (E x^2): no monotone map beats it.
Two rings: the best linear rule over 2000 directions reaches accuracy 0.722; an exact lift u' = |x| - 0.75 separates the classes with the plane u = 0 at accuracy 1.000.
Winding number: for 40 random planar flows the transported outer circle keeps winding number 1 about the inner circle's centre in every case: a planar flow cannot unlink the rings.
Learned decision regions: with no augmentation the regions have tendrils and accuracy 0.994 and 0.986 for two seeds; with one or four augmented dimensions they are smooth and accuracy is 1.000.

Animation and S003 stills: a learned flow of the rings in 3D with one augmented dimension at t = 0.22; and a before and after of augmenting a ring problem so that the two classes separate in the augmented coordinate (minimum u of one class above the maximum of the other).
read_the_figure.proves: Order preservation on the line and winding invariance in the plane are theorems about flows. A model class that is a flow inherits them, so it cannot represent maps that violate them; an extra dimension removes the obstruction. The figures show it with exact flows, and learned flows reproduce it.
if_wrong: A claim that a Neural ODE on the line fits a decreasing map: impossible for a flow.
A planar flow that appears to unlink rings: numerical error or crossing trajectories.
Augmentation without checking the augmented coordinate is initialized at a constant: otherwise it changes the problem.
Accuracy 1.000 reported without the decision regions: tendrils would show overfitting.
must_check: That the augmented dimensions and their initial values are stated.
That seeds are listed for learned results.
That the invariant being tested (order, winding number) is stated.
That exact lifts and learned flows are labelled differently.

terms.meaning: A flow on the line sends ordered points to ordered points.
The number of times a closed curve winds around a point; invariant under continuous deformation not crossing the point.
A Neural ODE with extra state coordinates, initialized at zero, added to the input.
An embedding of the data into a higher-dimensional space where the problem is easier.
A continuous invertible map with a continuous inverse; every flow map is one.

remember: The time-t map of an ODE is a homeomorphism.
In one dimension homeomorphisms that come from flows are increasing.
In the plane a flow cannot change the winding number of a curve about a point.
One augmented dimension suffices for the two-ring and the reversal problems.
A learned flow may also be fit without augmentation but with distorted decision regions.

steps.title: Why x to minus x is impossible on a line
steps.note: A continuous injective map of an interval is monotone. Flow maps are injective (uniqueness) and continuous; x to -x is monotone decreasing, but the flow map starts as the identity (increasing) and cannot become decreasing without a crossing.

steps.title: An exact augmented flow that reverses x
steps.tex: \begin{pmatrix}\dot x\\ \dot u\end{pmatrix}=\pi\begin{pmatrix}-u\\ x\end{pmatrix},\ u(0)=0\ \Rightarrow\ x(t)=x_0\cos\pi t,\ u(t)=x_0\sin\pi t,\ x(1)=-x_0
steps.note: Half circles: this is the middle panel. The augmented coordinate goes up and back to zero, so the map on x alone is x to -x.

steps.title: The best monotone approximation to x to minus x
steps.note: The minimum is at the constant (here zero), giving 1/3; the figure's 0.338 is the sample value for its sample of points.

steps.title: An exact lift that separates two rings
steps.tex: \dot u=|x|-0.75,\ u(0)=0\ \Rightarrow\ u(1)=|x|-0.75,\quad \text{inner ring }(|x|\approx0.3):\ u<0,\ \ \text{outer ring }(|x|\approx1):\ u>0
steps.note: The plane u = 0 separates the classes: the classifier is linear in (x, u). The flow does not move x and keeps the map a homeomorphism of the plane times a line.

worked.title: Separation by the exact lift
worked.problem: Rings of radius 0.3 and 1.0. Compute u(1) for each under u' = |x| - 0.75 and the margin.
worked.answer: The classes are separated by the plane u = 0 with a margin of 0.7 in the augmented coordinate.

analyze.q: In the left panel, why are there no curves ending at the red dots?
Why does the zero map equal the best nondecreasing fit?
analyze.hint: A decreasing target correlates negatively with any increasing map.

analyze.q: The winding number is 1 in all 40 flows. What does it say about the planar model class, not only about these 40?

evaluate.q: A learned model without augmentation reaches accuracy 0.994 on the rings. Is the obstruction wrong?
evaluate.hint: Tendrils: approximate separation by a distorted boundary.

evaluate.q: Is an augmented model a different model class? What does it cost in dimension and compute?

Predict how many augmented dimensions you need to unlink two linked rings in 3D.

checks.q: Why can two ODE trajectories not cross?
checks.answer: Through each point passes exactly one solution; a crossing would give two.

checks.q: The exact flow x(t) = x0 cos(pi t). x(1) for x0 = 0.8?
Why does augmentation work for the rings?
checks.answer: Points on the inner and outer rings can be moved apart in the extra coordinate without crossing paths in the plane, because curves do not meet in three dimensions the way they can in two.

checks.q: The learned decision regions have tendrils without augmentation. Is accuracy 0.994 convincing?
checks.answer: Not fully: the tendrils show a distorted boundary that may not generalize; the augmented models have smooth regions.

checks.q: Describe an experiment testing whether augmentation helps on a real task.
checks.answer: Compare the same Neural ODE with 0, 1 and several augmented dimensions over several seeds, reporting accuracy, regions and cost.
